title: Chatstream Replay Proxy: scalable SSE/WS load benchmark with p95 regression detection
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Build a replay-proxy based load harness that replays recorded real-client streaming chat sessions (SSE + WebSocket) at configurable token rates, session concurrency, and network conditions. The harness will focus on token/sec throughput, p95 token-delivery latency, p99 tail behavior, and automatic regression detection against a maintained baseline. Unlike earlier synthetic drivers, this proxy applies realistic token inter-arrival patterns, KV-cache warm/unwarm scenarios, and controlled client-side churn to reveal regressions that appear only under production-like streaming dynamics.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy can replay a corpus of recorded chat sessions over both SSE and WebSocket endpoints at target concurrency up to 20k concurrent streams
Metrics exported: tokens/sec (global and per-stream), p50/p95/p99 token delivery latency, connection success rate, average KV cache hit per session, and error classifications
Regression detector runs nightly: compares latest 7-day window p95 to baseline and raises an alert if p95 worsens by >20% with >100k tokens observed
Support for network emulation knobs: per-session RTT distribution, packet loss, and client send jitter
Integration with Grafana dashboard and Prometheus metrics (dash link in artifacts) and a GitHub actions job to run baseline smoke tests on PRs
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Recorder & corpus builder - instrument a lightweight client library to capture token timings and metadata for SSE/WS sessions (contrib script + sampling guidelines)
Phase 2: Replay proxy core - Go-based proxy that replays token events to Redwood endpoints, supports rate modulation and simultaneous multi-tenant routing
Phase 3: Network emulator - integrate netem-like controls to apply per-stream latency, jitter, and loss; support containerized runners for distributed scale
Phase 4: Observability + detector - emit standardized Prometheus metrics, build regression detector that stores daily summaries and runs threshold checks; wire alerts to PagerDuty channel
Phase 5: Scale validation - run phased scale tests (1k, 5k, 20k concurrent streams) and capture resource profiles to tune autoscaling recommendations
risks: Recorder bias: captured corpus might over-represent low-latency clients — mitigate with targeted sampling across regions
Proxy resource saturation: memory use when replaying many long-lived streams; design backpressure and bounded buffering
False positives in regression detector due to upstream infra changes — include changelog hooks and deployable baseline tagging
Security risk from storing recorded payloads — encrypt corpus at rest and scrub PII in recorder by default
notes: We intentionally avoid synthetic steady-token-rate generators. Real regressions often surface from token timing variance and cache warmup patterns.
Decision: implement proxy in Go for low-latency concurrency and re-use existing Redwood TLS stack. Trade-off: more engineering vs better performance fidelity compared to k6 or Node.js drivers.
We will reuse the ’stream-metrics’ Prometheus schema from ENG-21901 where possible to ease dashboarding and alerting cadence.

Work split: Marcus leads proxy + scale runs. Lena coordinates corpus collection and regression detector design. Priya Singh (PM) will validate acceptance criteria with SLO owners. Security review flagged for corpus storage and encryption
